title: Stored XSS via unsanitized whitelabeling `customCss` (`</style>` breakout) - enterprise-license-gated; patched in canary after v0.30.5
summary: ## Description ### Summary The enterprise "whitelabeling" feature stores an operator-supplied `customCss` string and injects it verbatim into a `` sequence in `customCss` closes the style element and allows arbitrary HTML/JS to follow (e.g. ``), yielding stored cross-site scripting. Because the whitelabeling config is served by the **public** `whitelabeling.getPublic` procedure and rendered on every page - including the unauthenticated login page - the payload executes in the browser of every visitor and user. **Important scope / severity caveat (validated):** both the write and the read of `customCss` are **enterprise-license-gated**. Setting it requires `whitelabeling.update` (an `enterpriseProcedure`), and the public render path (`getPublicWhitelabelingConfig`) returns `null` unless `hasAnyValidLicense()` is true. On an instance without a valid enterprise license this feature is inert and the vulnerability is **not exploitable** - so it primarily affects enterprise-licensed deployments, and the actor is a licensed instance owner/admin. This was fixed in the canary branch after v0.30.5. ### Details Sink - `apps/dokploy/components/proprietary/whitelabeling/whitelabeling-provider.tsx:29-33`: ```tsx {config?.customCss && ( ` renders as ``, and the `img` `onerror` executes. The live Content-Security-Policy is only `frame-ancestors 'none'` (no `script-src`), so inline event-handler script executes. **License gating (both paths):** - Write - `apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/proprietary/whitelabeling.ts:29`: `update: enterpriseProcedure` → without a license returns `403 "Valid enterprise license required"`. - Read - `packages/server/src/services/proprietary/whitelabeling.ts` `getPublicWhitelabelingConfig()`: ```ts export const getPublicWhitelabelingConfig = async () => { if (IS_CLOUD) return null; if (!(await hasAnyValidLicense())) return null; // <-- render path gated on license const settings = await getWebServerSettings(); const config = settings?.whitelabelingConfig; if (!config) return null; return { ..., customCss: config.customCss, ... }; }; ``` **Upstream fix (patch-gap):** commit `6282b6ef3` ("fix: resolve security vulnerabilities in whitelabeling"), landed on canary **after** the v0.30.5 release, adds `customCss.replace(/<\/style>/gi, "")` (and removes an SSR favicon SSRF). v0.30.5 does not contain this fix. ### PoC Confirmed on `dokploy/dokploy:v0.30.5` (git f67fab0), http://localhost:3000. This lab has **no enterprise license**, which - as shown below - makes the vulnerability non-exploitable here; on a licensed instance the same `customCss` value executes. **Payload (the stored XSS):** ``` ``` On a licensed instance an owner/admin sets it via the whitelabeling settings UI / API: ``` POST /api/whitelabeling.update {"customCss":""} ``` and it then renders (unsanitized) on every page served, including the unauthenticated login page, executing `alert(document.domain)` in each visitor's browser. **Live gating validation on this (unlicensed) instance - proving why a live popup is not demonstrable here:** 1) Owner attempts the write: ```bash curl -sS -i 'http://localhost:3000/api/whitelabeling.update' \ -H '...
